summary: Verified the Labour % by Revenue card was converted from a per-location BarChart to a time-series AreaChart that mirrors the Sales Trend pattern. Backend (sales.py) /api/admin/daily-sales/summary now returns a timeseries array where every row carries the new keys labour_hours and labour_cost (rounded 2dp) computed from staff_members.hourly_rate keyed by lowercase name. Frontend (admin-sales-summary/index.jsx) has an independent labourGranularity state with 4 toggle buttons (daily/weekly/monthly/yearly), rollUp() carries the new fields through buckets, and the card hides gracefully when no labour_cost > 0 in the range. All 7 backend tests pass and all 9 frontend assertions pass.
critical_code_review_comments: sales.py reuses the same staff_rate_map for both by_location and timeseries — single pass, no duplication. Good.

Lowercase name lookup is consistent — but a staff name typed as 'john' in daily_sales.staff_hours and 'John' in staff_members will still match. Document the case-insensitive contract or normalise at ingest.
Frontend rollUp() filter `labour_cost > 0 || sales > 0` drops buckets that are 0/0 — prevents a flat zero line on weekly/yearly views when only April has data. Sensible.

Card visibility is gated by `labourTrendData.some(r => r.labour_cost > 0)` — note this filters *after* the granularity rollup, so if the user picks 'yearly' on a non-April range the card may still render with the empty-state text; consider gating on data.timeseries instead so the empty-state copy isn't shown for the rare case of all-zero costs in some buckets. Cosmetic only.
ReferenceLine thresholds (28 / 35) match the header tinting thresholds in labourOverallPct color choice — single source of truth could be a small constant. Cosmetic.
